results.title: The geography of structural vulnerability: intersections of climate ...
results.content: Urban vulnerability to climate change is shaped not only by environmental exposure but also by structural inequalities embedded in the spatial distribution of ecological resources and economic capacity. This study develops a spatial framework for identifying structural vulnerability across urban and regional contexts by integrating three interrelated dimensions: heat stress, vegetation scarcity, and economic disadvantage. These include: (1) a green-constrained urban core, characterized by high heat stress, limited ecological buffering, and relatively strong economic resources; (2) a moderately vulnerable mixed-type with intermediate levels across all dimensions; (3) a green but economically disadvantaged type, where ecological benefits coexist with limited adaptive capacity; and (4) a low-stress, high-capacity cluster defined by favorable conditions across environmental and socioeconomic indicators. These include: (1) a green-constrained urban core—marked by severe heat and limited green infrastructure but relatively high economic capacity; (2) a moderately vulnerable mixed-type with average conditions across domains; (3) a green yet economically disadvantaged cluster, where ecological buffering is offset by limited material resources; and (4) a low-stress, high-capacity group with favorable conditions throughout.

results.title: Attachment and (in)securities. Threats to the notion of rootedness in ...
results.content: The residential insecurity hinder attachment to neighbourhood. The neighbourhood was once again shown as a space of roots where shared loyalties and social identities were formed and reinforced social cohesion and generated mutual support networks in response to an unprecedented situation such as the pandemic. These powerful links pose important challenges in a post-pandemic context, resulting from recent urban processes arising from the cost of housing and questioning the consolidation of proximity, the concept of neighbourhood as community and the right to housing. Based on analysis of 20 in-depth semi-structured interviews were conducted in two neighbourhoods (Montbau and Sant Antoni) and preceded by an analysis of secondary data related to residential (in)stability and mobility this article to explore the sense of belonging, community dynamics and the social cohesion. This research confirms two types of threats: a) recent urban processes that promote residential insecurity and, b) community dynamics that hinder integration and bonds. Obstructing neighbourhood ties breaks the social protection network.
